assets.name: Water Tower
assets.kind: Lost structure · gravity-fed every campus building
assets.version: Reconstruction 002 · MZ.Claude · 2026-11-07 · from the c.1971 photograph (replaces the first-pass placeholder)
assets.stats: ≈32 m to the finial · tank ≈6.7 m across · 4 legs, 9.7 m apart on the diagonal at the footings · 3.2k triangles
assets.summary: Built beside Farm Road after the Allan Building was finished. A waterwheel in the pump house on the Gwynns Falls mill race lifted 30,000–40,000 gallons a day to its tank, and every campus building was fed by gravity. Taken down in June 1987 after the school moved to city water. Rebuilt from the archive photograph John Aaron shared: a four-post tapered lattice tower with two strut rings and rod cross-bracing, a central riser pipe, a cylindrical tank on a rounded bottom, a walkway with a rail, a cone roof with a ball finial, and a ladder. Someone painted "2nd EFFORT '71" on the tank.

placement.detail: 1938 US Coast & Geodetic Survey position agrees within 4 m with MZ.Human's GPS on the surviving south footing (4 Nov 2026). Legs set on the compass points so one stands at the south footing; the model puts that footing 4.9 m from the centre, the GPS put it 4.1 m (±9.5 m). Heading not yet measured.

sources.title: The water tower, c.1971 ("2nd EFFORT '71" painted on the tank)
sources.who: McDonogh School archives · in John Aaron's "G2 Oct. 2022 – Growth in McD History" deck
sources.used: The whole form: four tapered posts, two strut rings, rod X-bracing in every panel, central riser with joint bands, cylinder on a rounded bottom, walkway with rail and brackets, cone roof with ball finial, ladder. Proportions measured from the image: three near-equal panels below the tank, cylinder about half a panel tall, outer legs at the top about as wide as the tank (seen on the diagonal). Absolute size is scaled, not surveyed.

assets.name: McDonogh Station
assets.kind: Lost building · Western Maryland Railroad stop, the boys' connection to home
assets.stats: ≈20 m with the service wing · 2 storeys · ridge ≈10 m · 3.9k triangles
assets.summary: The Western Maryland Railroad stop about a mile from the school. From November 1873 boys rode the train from Fulton Station to here; Visiting Days filled it with families, and in 1912 a special train was added. After service ended it became home to the family of one of the bus drivers, and it is believed to have been demolished to make way for I-795. Modelled as the board-and-batten Gothic station of the cyanotype: two storeys, a cross gable over the track-side waiting porch, finials, three chimneys, a one-storey service wing and woodshed.

placement.detail: Placed on machine find C11 (a 12 × 20 m sunken rectangle), identified as the station site by MZ.Human, 5 Nov 2026. Track side faces east toward the rail corridor. Open question for a field check: today's corridor floor is about 4 m below C11 and about 30 m east, while the photographs show the platform level with the track.
